newsitem.title: GERMANY: FOCUS-Waigel says will try to make peace with bank.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Waigel says will try to make peace with bank.

text.p: German Finance Minister Theo Waigel said on Monday he would try to reach agreement with the Bundesbank before proposing legal changes to revalue its assets in a bid to qualify for European monetary union (EMU).

Waigel said that the Bundesbank was already in general agreement with the plan, despite the objections it has voiced. The main difference is over whether the revaluation would take effect this year or next, he said.
But he added he would proceed with the government's plan to change the central bank law even without the Bundesbank's assent.
Waigel said he believed the Bundesbank would be open to a revaluation of its assets in 1998, if not this year.

"We will discuss this with the Bundesbank" in the next few days, he told reporters after a meeting of leaders of his Christian Social Union (CSU) political party. "We will try to do this in mutual agreement."
Bonn hopes the revaluation of the central bank's assets could help Germany meet the EMU criteria by generating an extraordinary profit that would be passed along to the government.
The plan has led to an unusually open split between Chancellor Helmut Kohl and Bundesbank president Hans Tietmeyer, who has said the plan would threaten the stability of the future single currency.

Waigel said that even without a revaluation of the Bundesbank assets, Germany's outstanding debt is only slightly above the target level for European monetary union of 60 percent of gross domestic product.
